name: The Realms in Exile
description: The Númenórean exiles establish the kingdoms of Arnor and Gondor in Middle-earth following the Downfall of Númenor.
extra: Elendil the Tall and his sons Isildur and Anárion lead the Faithful to Middle-earth, bringing with them the palantíri and a seedling of the White Tree.
The kingdoms are founded: Arnor in the north under Elendil, and Gondor in the south under Isildur and Anárion.
These realms represent the last great kingdoms of Men in Middle-earth, preserving Númenórean culture and knowledge.

name: The Last Alliance
description: The Last Alliance of Elves and Men is formed to combat the growing threat of Sauron in Mordor.
extra: Gil-galad, High King of the Noldor, and Elendil, High King of Arnor and Gondor, lead their combined forces against Sauron.
The Alliance marches to Mordor, laying siege to Barad-dûr for seven years.
In the final confrontation on the slopes of Mount Doom, both Gil-galad and Elendil are slain, but Sauron is overthrown when Isildur cuts the One Ring from his hand.

name: Disaster of the Gladden Fields
description: Isildur and his three eldest sons are slain by Orcs at the Gladden Fields, and the One Ring is lost.
extra: While traveling to Arnor, Isildur's company is ambushed by a vast host of Orcs in the Vales of Anduin.
Isildur attempts to escape by using the Ring's power of invisibility, but it slips from his finger in the Great River, and he is killed by Orc arrows.
The Ring lies hidden in the riverbed for over two thousand years, until it is found by Déagol and claimed by Sméagol.

name: Arnor Broken
description: The kingdom of Arnor is divided into three separate realms following the death of King Eärendur.
extra: The sons of Eärendur quarrel over the succession, and the kingdom is split into Arthedain, Cardolan, and Rhudaur.
This division weakens the North Kingdom significantly, making it vulnerable to future threats.
The line of Isildur continues through the kings of Arthedain, while the other kingdoms eventually fall into ruin.

name: The Rise of Angmar
description: The Witch-king establishes the realm of Angmar in the north, threatening the remnants of Arnor.
extra: A dark realm arises in the northern wastes, ruled by the chief of the Nazgûl, who becomes known as the Witch-king of Angmar.
Angmar begins a long war against the Dúnedain kingdoms, particularly targeting Arthedain, Cardolan, and Rhudaur.
This marks the beginning of a centuries-long conflict that will ultimately lead to the destruction of the North Kingdom.

name: The Fall of Amon Sûl
description: The watchtower of Amon Sûl is destroyed by forces from Angmar, and the palantír is saved by King Arveleg I.
extra: Angmar launches a major assault on Arthedain, capturing and destroying the ancient watchtower of Weathertop.
King Arveleg I is slain in the defense of Amon Sûl, but the palantír is rescued and taken to Fornost.
Cardolan is overrun and falls into ruin, while Rhudaur becomes a vassal of Angmar.

name: The Kin-Strife
description: A bloody civil war erupts in Gondor over the succession, lasting five years.
extra: The conflict begins when Castamir the Usurper overthrows King Eldacar, who was born of a mother from Rhovanion.
Castamir's brutal rule and the burning of Osgiliath turn many against him.
Eldacar returns with an army, defeats Castamir at the Battle of the Crossings of Erui, and reclaims the throne, but Gondor is permanently weakened.

name: The Great Plague
description: A devastating plague sweeps across Middle-earth, decimating populations in both Gondor and Arnor.
extra: The plague originates in the east and spreads rapidly westward, killing vast numbers.
In Gondor, King Telemnar and all his children perish, and the capital Osgiliath is largely abandoned.
In the north, the last remnants of Cardolan are destroyed, and the watch on Mordor is abandoned.

name: The Disaster of the Morannon
description: King Ondoher of Gondor and both his sons are slain in battle against the Wainriders.
extra: Gondor faces a two-pronged invasion: the Wainriders from the east and the Haradrim from the south.
King Ondoher leads his army north to meet the Wainriders but is overwhelmed and killed along with both his sons.
General Eärnil rallies the southern army, defeats the Haradrim, then marches north to destroy the Wainriders at the Battle of the Camp, saving Gondor from conquest.

name: The Ride of Eorl
description: Eorl the Young leads his people from the north to aid Gondor, and the Rohirrim are granted the land of Calenardhon.
extra: Gondor is invaded by a massive host of Orcs and Easterlings who overrun Calenardhon and threaten to destroy the northern army.
Eorl answers Gondor's call for aid, leading his cavalry in a legendary ride from the north.
At the Battle of the Field of Celebrant, Eorl's riders turn the tide of battle, routing the invaders and saving Gondor.

name: The Long Winter
description: A catastrophic winter grips Middle-earth, bringing famine and hardship to Rohan and beyond.
extra: The Long Winter lasts nearly five months, from November to March, with snow covering the land.
Rohan is simultaneously invaded by Dunlendings and Easterlings, led by Wulf, who captures Edoras.
King Helm Hammerhand retreats to the Hornburg, where he and his people endure a siege through the terrible winter. Helm dies in the cold, but his nephew Fréaláf retakes Edoras in the spring.

name: The War of the Dwarves and Orcs
tooltip: The War of the Dwarves and Orcs
description: The Dwarves wage a brutal war against the Orcs of the Misty Mountains to avenge Thrór.
extra: King Thrór of Durin's Folk is murdered by the Orc Azog in Moria, sparking outrage among all the Dwarf clans.
A confederation of Dwarven armies hunts down and destroys Orc strongholds throughout the Misty Mountains.
The war culminates in the Battle of Azanulbizar at the gates of Moria, where the Dwarves achieve a costly victory but do not reclaim their ancient home.

name: The Quest for Erebor
description: Thorin Oakenshield and his company, accompanied by Bilbo Baggins, journey to the Lonely Mountain to reclaim their homeland from Smaug.
extra: Gandalf orchestrates the quest, seeing the threat that Smaug poses if Sauron should ally with the dragon.
Bilbo discovers the One Ring in the tunnels beneath the Misty Mountains during the journey.
The quest succeeds when Smaug is slain, but it leads directly to the Battle of Five Armies and the deaths of Thorin, Fíli, and Kíli.

name: The War of the Ring
description: The final confrontation between the Free Peoples and Sauron begins with the discovery that the One Ring has been found.
extra: Sauron has rebuilt his power in Mordor and is preparing to crush the last kingdoms of Men.
In Gondor, Steward Denethor II fortifies his realm against the coming storm, while his sons Boromir and Faramir defend the borders.
To the south, the Haradrim and Corsairs of Umbar prepare to strike at Gondor's vulnerable coastline.
In Rohan, King Théoden faces threats from Isengard as Saruman the White makes his fateful choice.
The fate of Middle-earth hangs in the balance as the quest to destroy the Ring begins.

name: The Fourth Age
description: The beginning of the Dominion of Men, as the Elves depart Middle-earth and the kingdoms of Gondor and Arnor are reunited.
extra: King Elessar (Aragorn) rules the Reunited Kingdom in peace and prosperity.
The Shire is recognized and protected under the King's authority, entering a golden age.
The Elves continue their journey west across the Sea, leaving Middle-earth to the dominion of Men.
